title: What happens when you call an API?

candidates.hook: A hungry diner waves a menu while a small waiter bursts through a clattering, steaming kitchen door with a covered plate.
candidates.scene: A diner at a restaurant table orders from a menu, and a waiter carries the order to a kitchen the diner never sees.

steps.analogy: The diner reads the menu to see what's allowed
The diner picks one dish and the waiter takes it away

The waiter returns with the dish as described
An off-menu ask gets a polite 'we don't have that'

candidates.visual: A cartoon cafe table, a big menu, a small waiter, and a swinging kitchen door with steam puffing out.
candidates.process: The diner can only ask for what the menu lists. They point at one dish and the waiter takes that order to the kitchen. The kitchen does all the cooking out of sight, using its own methods. The waiter brings back the finished dish exactly as the menu described it. If the diner asks for something not on the menu, the waiter returns with a polite refusal. The diner never needs to know how any dish was made.

elements.name: the diner at the table
elements.stands_for: the client program that wants something done

candidates.process: The keypad offers only certain codes, so the shopper can only ask in those ways. They press a code and the hidden mechanism turns, finds the right item, and drops it. The item always arrives in the same tray, in the same predictable form. If the shopper presses a code that's sold out, the machine beeps and gives back nothing. The shopper never learns how the spiral or motor works.

The driver turns the wheel

The car turns as expected

candidates.visual: A cheerful cartoon car shown from the side with the hood popped open on glowing gears, and a small driver at the wheel.
candidates.process: The driver can only use the controls the car offers: turn, accelerate, brake. Each control sends a clear instruction into the machinery, which does all the complicated work under the hood. The car then visibly responds by turning or speeding up. Different drivers can use the same controls on any model of car without knowing how the engine is built. There is no pedal for something the car cannot do.
